title: Semilinear compact-support exchange is site reindexing
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient conventions of [def-pur-conventions]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism of separated finite-type $k$-schemes, let $g:Y'\xrightarrow{\sim}Y$ be an isomorphism of underlying schemes, and form its Cartesian square with $f':X'\to Y'$ and $g':X'\xrightarrow{\sim}X$ [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. No $k$-linearity of $g,g'$ is required. Choose a compactification $c=(X\xrightarrow j\overline X\xrightarrow pY)$ and its base change $c'=(j',p')$, with induced isomorphism $\bar g:\overline X'\xrightarrow{\sim}\overline X$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. On the domains of [def-exchange-projection], use its specified unit--square--counit exchange and canonical open comparison, over $S=Y$. Its map
$$\operatorname{Ex}_!^c:L g^*Rp_*j_!\longrightarrow Rp'_*j'_!L g'^*$$
is precisely the natural isomorphism
$$g^{-1}Rp_*j_!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp'_*\bar g^{-1}j_!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp'_*j'_!g'^{-1}$$
induced by the site reindexing equivalences of [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image]; completed pullback along these isomorphisms has the same identification. The first factor is the specified direct-image mate, not a separately chosen comparison. These maps respect identity and successive isomorphism base changes and vertical composition of the compactifiable maps, under the canonical direct-image, open-extension and compact-support composition comparisons. On finite constructible finite-Tor inputs they commute with derived quotient-coefficient extension; they also commute with integral reduction, rationalization and common-stage coefficient extension on the specified coefficient domains. The integral comparisons are formed on the actual strict reduction towers using [def-cbc-completed-exchange-map], before $R\lim$; the rational and algebraically closed comparisons are their scalar-localized/common-stage images. For maps and objects in the compactification-independent field-base domains of [fix-lem-exchanges], insert those canonical compactification comparisons in the displayed identity.

proof.text: Over $S=Y$, apply [lem-pur-isomorphism-finite-mate-normalization] to the chosen compactification and its isomorphism pullback. It identifies the specified proper mate with $r$ and the specified open factor with $\beta$. Hence $\operatorname{Ex}_!^c=Rp'_*(\beta)r_{j_!-}$ is exactly the displayed natural reindexing isomorphism at finite coefficients, including the normalization of its first factor.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-isomorphism-finite-exchange-coherence] to these finite maps: its identity and horizontal equations give identity and successive base changes; its vertical-interchange equation gives compatibility with compactifiable composition, inserting the canonical compositors. Its quotient-coefficient square gives the claimed finite coefficient compatibility on constructible finite-Tor inputs.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-completed-reindexing-lifted-coefficients], which specializes the coefficient-independent module, limit and mate argument to pbcIntegralDatum. The coefficient prime is a unit on every k-scheme. The pointwise clause gives completed reindexing, and the square clause gives the specified ordinary and strict mates on each supplied chosen Cartesian square.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-isomorphism-strict-integral-exchange-normalization] to $M=j_!K$ on the supplied integral domain. Its strict equality $v_\bullet=r_\bullet$ identifies the actual chosen lift before $R\lim$. Its reconstruction identity then gives the same ordered proper/open reindexing composite for the completed exchange. Its strict pasting and reduction equations give the integral identity, horizontal and vertical composition, and integral reduction claims. For invertibility of the completed exchange, the proper normalization makes the source completion unit invertible, and the open normalization makes the target completion unit invertible. The ordinary reindexing exchange is the composite of the invertible proper mate and direct image of the open comparison. Its normalized total identity therefore makes the completed exchange invertible by cancellation of the source unit.

proof.text: The hypotheses of [lem-pur-isomorphism-exchange-scalar-refinement-descent] are precisely the finite identifications and equations from Steps 1--2 and the completed identifications and strict equations from Steps 3--4. Its scalar conclusions give rationalization and common-stage coefficient extension with the same ordered identity. Its refinement equation inserts the canonical compactification comparisons on the stated field-base domains and intertwines the canonical composition comparisons there. Its six outputs are the predicates of [def-pur-semilinear-exchange-descent-data].
